why:
I checked all three must_catch items against the two briefs, and each one is handled.

(1) The trap is flagged outside any PASS/FAIL condition. The verifier's Advisory says "Returning {} hides which file is broken and where, which goes against the need stated in the issue body". It also says `node src/app.js <bad file>` "will now start with the defaults instead of exiting 1". Builder step 4 makes the same point: the app "starts... with defaults instead of printing `bad config:`". Builder step 6 asks for this to be noted in the PR.

(2) The builder changes the existing test. Builder step 3 replaces the 'bad JSON throws' test with one that asserts deepEqual {} and no throw. Step 5 then runs npm test.

(3) The verifier's line-1 check uses invalid JSON. Check 1 writes `{port: 9000` to a file, calls loadConfig on it, and PASSes when the call doesn't throw and prints `{} true`, meaning it returned an empty plain object.
